2. FBL 4.7 and 4.6: a comment after a brace or a statement (B3, B4)
**Construct.** FBL 4.7 opens a block only when a statement's last non-whitespace character is the brace, so `model { // …` opens none and the braces

3. FBL: a comment that spans lines (B5)
**Construct.** The tool skips `/* … */`, within a line and across lines. FBL has no comment that spans lines: the lines inside one are statements, a
**Shown by.** `findings/block-comments.dsl`.
**Would resolve it.** `blockComment: {open, close}` on a binding.
**Meanwhile.** As gap 1.
4. FBL: an escape inside a quoted group (B7)
**Construct.** The tool reads `\"` inside a quoted argument as a quote and writes a quote back escaped. FBL has escaping rules for XML, YAML and
**Shown by.** `findings/escaped-quote.dsl`; the transcript's renames to `Parity "name"`.
**Would resolve it.** An escape for a quoted group, read and written.
**Meanwhile.** The module's commands write every edit.

8. FBL: adding a block, and a value gathered from two places (B24, B9)

**Shown by.** `findings/tags-in-block.dsl` for the tags; for the view block, the transcript's `add view` steps, which every document of the corpus

**Construct.** A view's `autoLayout` sets the layout's direction and its rank and node separation (top to bottom, 120 and 60 otherwise), and a view

15. DISL 3.5 and 6.13: the order of a view's members and of its legend entries
**Construct.** The tool draws, lays out and keys a view's members in the order of the statements that select them: what the view's `include`

**Meanwhile.** The module orders the members it reads from the model by the view's statements, and keys the legend by them, each entry painted from
**The canvas.** How big a card is, the `c4Ranks` arrangement, the boundary drawn around a container or component view's scope and around a hosting
**An element declared without an identifier** is named `<kind>_<name>_<n>` by the host for the session, n counting such elements in document order,
**The host's own refusals**, which come from the wire rather than from an operation: "'<action id>' does not apply to this selection." for an action
items.reason: These refusals answer a request the host's wire carries, an action id, a property id or an element id, that names nothing the description offers for the selection; mapping a gesture onto an intent the description names is the host's, and the writer's two refusals are the reader's (binding structurizr).

items.text: **Prompts.** A rename or relabel prompt may be drawn in place of the element's name or the line's label. The prompt's validation refuses a blank name
items.reason: Where a rename or relabel prompt is drawn, and its refusal of a blank name while it is typed, are how the host takes the operation's parameter; the operation itself refuses nothing more.

items.text: **Styles.** The `styles` block's headers are recorded and its properties never read, so a document's styles change nothing; the definition states the
**`c4/code`** keeps its registration and its refusing factory, and has no definition.

hostCode.behaviour: The workspace is read line by line, a comment after a statement or a brace and a comment spanning lines skipped and a body whose braces do not balance read as far as it balances, every element and relationship whichever view is shown, an element without an identifier named `<kind>_<name>_<n>`.

The views block's statements are read view by view: the key, the scope, a deployment view's environment, `include`, `exclude`, `title`, `autoLayout` with its direction and separations, and a dynamic view's interactions in their order.
A body is read without its byte order mark, which a write puts back; a body that cannot be read is unreadable and refuses every edit.
The findings are listed element by element: the includes, then each element's, then each relationship's, then each view's, then the coverage findings.

Each finding's condition and sentence: an element's missing description and technology, an element nothing connects, one placed in the wrong parent, a relationship whose end names nothing, a view whose scope names nothing and an empty view.

A view's members: what its `include` statements name, in their order, then what `include *` adds within the kinds it permits, then a dynamic view's interactions' ends, less what it excludes and the element it is inside of.
A relationship whose ends are not both drawn is lifted to the nearest drawn ancestor of each end, one line per pair of drawn elements, the first relationship on the pair giving its label.
The title drawn above the view: the declared title, else one made from the view's kind and the name of what it is scoped to, a landscape naming the workspace and a deployment view its environment.
What the canvas is sent: the drawn elements within the viewport, as payloads of the host's types, with the synthetic ids `c4:view` and `boundary:<id>`.
hostCode.reason: The payloads, the viewport filter and the ids of what only the canvas draws are how this host draws a scene; the description names what is drawn.

hostCode.behaviour: Each card's background and text colour by kind, muted for an external element, and the swatch of each legend entry; a document's styles change nothing.

A view's members ranked by the longest path along the relationships (a dynamic view's interactions), each rank a row centred on the others, `autoLayout`'s direction and separations replacing top to bottom 120 and 60 and making stored positions ignored, a stored position replacing the computed one otherwise.
A deployment view nests every node around what it hosts, to any depth, each set of siblings ranked on its own; a stored position is honoured only for an element no node encloses.
A container or component view's boundary around its scope's children, and every other element that overlaps it moved out by its shortest route and then separated from the others moved out.
Each card's size, from its name, type line and description measured with the module's font metric.
hostCode.reason: How wide a text is and how many lines a description wraps onto are the host's measurement; the layout takes each card's size as its input.

hostCode.behaviour: The box a card occupies: as wide as its widest line within 160 to 240, as tall as the lines its description wraps onto.
hostCode.reason: The estimate of a text's width is the host's font metric.

hostCode.behaviour: A new element's identifier: the letters and digits of its name, the first lowered, `_` before a leading digit and `element` when nothing is left, then `web2`, `web3` against an identifier in use.
A container is added only inside a software system and a component only inside a container, each refused elsewhere in its sentence; the deployment kinds are not added from the toolbox.
A new element's declaration is written into the block of the element it goes in, a block opened on a parent that has none.
Setting a name, description or technology rewrites the one line that declares it, writing `""` for each absent argument before the one set.
Positions live in `<base>.layout.json`, keyed by view and by element compared without regard to case, each number as .NET writes a double.
A new body is a workspace named after its file with a placeholder software system and one view of the reading's kind that includes everything and lays out left to right.
The toolbox of each kind of view: the kinds it permits, each with its label, icon and description.

A drag never changes what contains an element ("Dragging changes where an element is drawn, not what contains it."), and a move on a view that names nothing is refused ("This diagram has no view to arrange.").
hostCode.reason: A drag is a gesture the host maps onto a move of a position; that a drag onto another element is no reparent is that mapping.
